Turning anything into Jot

ON THIS PAGE

Notes in a phone app, a chat with a friend, meeting minutes, a spreadsheet of sleep hours, an Obsidian vault, a photographed page: most of what you would want in a journal already exists somewhere else. This guide covers two helpers for bringing it into Jot: an agent skill that tells an AI coding agent how to write good Jot, and jot check, which says whether a file is valid.

Check any .jot file

jot check reads one or more journals and lists anything the Jot rules would trip over, one line each, with where it is:

node cli/jot.mjs check october.jot notes.jot
october.jot:41:1 error unclosed-record Record consumes through end of file. Add ::: to close it.
2 files: 1 error, 0 warnings
  • An error (an unclosed :::record, the same record id twice) makes it exit with 1, so a script or a CI job can stop.
  • A warning (a date that does not exist, like 2026-02-30) is listed but still passes; add --strict to fail on warnings too.
  • --json prints the same list as JSON. Packaged .jotz journals are read too.

Nothing is changed and nothing leaves your computer.

The to-jot agent skill

The Jot project includes a skill called to-jot: written instructions an AI agent follows when you ask it to turn something into a journal, generate a new template, or fix an invalid Jot file. It lives in the project at .agents/skills/to-jot/, where OpenAI's Codex finds skills, and Claude Code finds the same folder through .claude/skills/to-jot. There is one copy, so both agents work the same way.

Open the Jot project in either agent and ask in your own words:

  • "Create an undated daily check-in template and validate the saved file."
  • "Turn chat-export.txt into a jot."
  • "Make a journal from these meeting notes, one entry per meeting."
  • "Import sleep.csv into 2026-10.jot."

The skill tells the agent to:

  1. Use Jot's own tools first: the converter for plain-text diaries (Converting an old diary) and jot import for numbers in a CSV (Automation and connections).
  2. Write the rest by hand in Jot's form: a ### YYYY-MM-DD | Weekday heading for each day, tasks, events, questions and ideas marked only where the material clearly has them, and numbers in records only where the value is written down.
  3. Escape any line that would accidentally read as a Jot mark (o well, never mind becomes \o well, never mind).
  4. Run jot check --strict on the final saved file and fix every error and warning before saying it is validated.

Describe it, or build it through a conversation

You do not need to know Jot's syntax. Ask for what you want:

  • “Make a gentle weekly planner with space for meals and one small priority.”
  • “Interview me and create a journal template that fits how I write.”
  • “Ask me about my day, then turn my answers into a Jot entry.”

The agent can draft directly from your brief or ask one short question at a time. You can skip questions, change the direction, or say “make it now”. A template has blank answers; a filled entry uses only the experiences you describe. Once it has enough information, the agent writes the file, validates it, and lets you revise it without learning the file format.

What the skill will not do

  • Invent anything. No guessed dates, years, times, numbers or units. Notes without a date stay undated, at the top before the first day (a dated entry runs on until the next date, so anything below it would take its date). A weekday like "Thursday" is turned into a date only when the material itself pins it down, and a margin note says so.
  • Rewrite you. Your words stay as they were: no summarising, tidying or translating unless you ask.
  • Diagnose. It records what was written or measured, never what it might mean.
  • Send your writing anywhere else. The skill reaches no service. The agent you use does read the material, so its provider's privacy terms apply; keep anything you would not share out of the folder you ask about.

What comes out

A messy chat, for example:

[2026-10-20 09:14] Robin: are we still on for the pottery class thursday?
[2026-10-20 09:16] Me: yes!! 6:30pm right?
[2026-10-20 09:20] Me: TODO buy apron
? what do I do with the wonky bowl

becomes:

## Undated

? what do I do with the wonky bowl

### 2026-10-20 | Tuesday

- **Robin** (09:14): are we still on for the pottery class thursday?
- **Me** (09:16): yes!! 6:30pm right?
- **Me** (09:20): TODO buy apron

[ ] buy apron

### 2026-10-22 | Thursday

o 6:30pm Pottery class

[[ date from "thursday" in the 20 October messages ]]

The skill's reference/ folder has this example in full, a CSV of sleep hours and an undated brain dump, each with the original beside the result, and a one-page summary of Jot's marks.

Pictures, photographed pages and PDFs

The agent transcribes only what it can read and marks the rest [illegible]. To keep the original picture with the writing, the journal becomes a packaged .jotz, with an attachment record that describes the picture in words:

:::record attachment #page-2026-10-20
path: assets/page-2026-10-20.jpg
media-type: image/jpeg
alt: A page of handwritten notes with a sketch of a mug
ocr-status: unreviewed
:::

Open the .jot in the workspace (Write) and attach the pictures there, and it saves the .jotz for you.

Validate from any directory

The skill includes a strict validation helper. Replace the skill path with its installed location:

node /path/to/to-jot/scripts/validate.mjs /path/to/journal.jot
node /path/to/to-jot/scripts/validate.mjs --json /path/to/journal.jot

It uses the same parser and package checks as jot check --strict, requires Node.js 22 or later, and needs no npm install. The downloadable skill bundles the validator; a repository installation finds the project automatically. An installed copy without that runtime can use --repo /path/to/.jot. Errors and warnings fail validation. Missing tools are reported as a setup failure.

A successful check proves that the parser/package checks passed. The agent must also review source fidelity, dates, units and method profile fields; parser success alone does not establish factual correctness or full profile compliance.
